payload.summary: Accepted 2 of 5 amendments after code verification. The co2_aq_mmol_per_l backward-compatibility regression and the invalid non-finite test are real issues. Rejected 3: the dead-code amendment is not a defect; the ProcessParams rename is actually complete (all cited files use new names); and the legacy migration does handle all 8 decomposer/nitrifier fields correctly in both save.rs and presets.rs.

votes.rationale: Verified that conversions.rs is unused outside its test module. However, this is preparatory infrastructure for a documented unit policy (UNITS.md), not a correctness, safety, or compatibility defect. The module is declared `pub mod` so clippy dead_code lint won't fire. No build breakage, no behavioral bug, no safety issue. Agree with planner position.

Verified: TankSnapshotRepr has co2_aq_mmol_per_l: f64 with no #[serde(default)] and no entry in LEGACY_SNAPSHOT_CHEMISTRY_FIELD_ALIASES. Any snapshot JSON serialized before this field was added will fail deserialization with a missing-field error. This is a real backward-compatibility regression requiring #[serde(default)] or a legacy alias entry.

Factually incorrect. Verified all cited locations: tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:347-389 uses the new names (decomposer_k_doc_mg_c_per_l, aob_k_tan_mg_n_per_l, etc.); cycling.rs:467 uses decomposer_k_do_mg_per_l; cycling.rs:505 uses decomposer_k_doc_mg_c_per_l; cycling.rs:637-641 all use new names. The Explore agent confirmed the project builds successfully. The rename is complete and consistent across the entire codebase.

Factually incorrect. Verified save.rs:749-776 (migrate_v9_to_v10) explicitly converts all 8 decomposer/nitrifier half-saturation fields using legacy_total_param_to_mg_per_l (divides by 20.0L reference volume). Presets.rs:1264-1287 does the same for TOML presets. The amendment claims 'the save migration chain only converts plant/algae half-saturation keys' but this is wrong — both plant/algae (v8→v9) and decomposer/nitrifier (v9→v10) migrations exist and perform proper unit conversion.

Verified: TankSnapshot::from_state recomputes pH via projected_carbonate_equilibrium() (snapshot.rs:240), which uses DIC and alkalinity — NOT state.water.ph. Furthermore, clamp_carbonate_ph() in chemistry.rs converts any non-finite pH to 7.0. Setting state.water.ph = NaN will never produce a NaN in the snapshot, so the test assertion will fail (violations will be empty). The test must exercise a field that passes through to the snapshot unchanged.
